04c87e3be1eaafbe4ed9f5ea95388d1a20ccb91f: The largest ski area in the world, and that's not just a slogan: 600 km of runs that link up without ever needing the car, from Courchevel to Val Thorens via Méribel and Les Menuires. Originally three valleys – Saint-Bon, Allues, Belleville – joined by Orelle on the Maurienne side. This is the kingdom of high-altitude skiing: Val Thorens peaks at 2,300 m in the village, the Cime Caron tops 3,200 m, and the snow lasts from November to May. Each resort has its own distinct personality, from the unapologetic luxury of Courchevel 1850 to the family spirit of Les Menuires. Plan on several days: nobody skis around the whole area in a single day.
04cfe0cb229809e2a4b9edb78280bca57859c891: Larche is a small-scale resort — 2 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts at all. Larche has kept the identity of an authentic mountain village, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. Here, people come for clean air, unspoiled landscapes and a friendly atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialisation of skiing in some large ski areas. Larche's altitude (1700 m at the base, 2200 m at the top) allows it to maintain decent snow cover in mid-winter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it is best to check conditions before finalising a booking. With a day lift pass at just 18€, Larche is one of the most affordable destinations in France. For families on a tight budget or skiers who want to make the most of their days without breaking the bank, it is a sincere and often overlooked choice. In short: Larche does not compete with the giants of skiing and makes no such claim. It is an honest, often underrated destination that deserves to be (re)discovered.
